Control stream of derivatives for the linearization of a base model

Source: R/nm_optimize_base.R
nm_derivatives_ctl.Rd

Writes a copy of a base control stream that evaluates the model once at the final estimates (MAXEVAL=0, all parameters FIX) and tabulates, for every record, the individual prediction and the derivatives of Y with respect to the ETAs (G_ETAk), the EPSs (H_EPSj) and the cross derivatives (D_EPSj_ETAk, interaction). The derivatives are read through verbatim code (G(k,1), HH(j,1), HH(j,k+1) in $ERROR; G and H in $PRED) placed at the end of the block ("LAST), as in the PsN linearize tool. The table is the input of level 2 of nm_optimize_base().

Usage

nm_derivatives_ctl(run, output_dir = NULL, name = NULL, extra = NULL, ...)

Arguments

run

Run directory of the base model (e.g. "run1.reg") or path prefix ("dir/run1") whose .ctl and .ext files are used.

output_dir

Directory of the new control stream (formerly out_dir, still accepted with a warning). Default: the analysis directory (parent of a .reg/.nm7 run directory), so that the $DATA path keeps the convention of nm_run().

name

Name of the new run. Default "<run>_deriv".

extra

Additional data items to tabulate (e.g. an occasion column "OCC" for inter-occasion variability). Items absent from $INPUT are dropped with a warning.

...

Former argument name, accepted with a warning until version 1.0: out_dir (now output_dir).

Value

Invisibly, the path of the control stream written. The table file is <name>.dtab.

Details

Not testable without NONMEM: the verbatim code follows the NONMEM help (ERROR: G(i,1) is the partial derivative of F with respect to ETA(i); HH(j,1) with respect to EPS(j); HH(j,i+1) the second derivative with respect to EPS(j) and ETA(i)). Models with F_FLAG (M3 likelihood) or simulation-only records are not supported.

See also

nm_optimize_base()
